issues.description: Code.do reads six named raw files that are absent from the package: the hand-collected workbook, currency CSV, Compustat Global gzip file, FAME DTA, I/B/E/S EPS International file, and Audit Analytics Europe fee CSV. The package's only data file is a registration-number list and Code.do does not read it. The assigned frozen catalog has native global Compustat and I/B/E/S candidates with successful one-row reads, and an Audit Analytics Europe fee/company candidate pair; those are not yet verified for period, population, transformations or every handoff. No FAME or exact raw-file catalog entry was found. Hand-workbook field ownership, currency quote/history, vendor-source mappings and required observation coverage remain unresolved before the 2.1.dta -> 2.2.a.dta -> FINAL.dta chain is closed.

The entry script changes to an absolute Mac user directory that is not part of this release. The DATA-relative paths can be preserved by staging the expected DATA tree under a dedicated writable run root, setting home_directory to '.', and launching Code.do in batch mode from that root.

The frozen header and datasheet identify Audit Implications of Non-GAAP Reporting, while the included online appendix identifies itself as U.S. Auditor Materiality Decisions and describes a U.S. audit-partner survey. Retain the registered title/DOI and the Code.do workflow as imported; ask the depositor to confirm whether this appendix belongs in this package before attributing its contents to the registered paper. The appendix is not used as an input or analysis entry point for the supplied Code.do target.

The supplied currency CSV is absent. Code.do says the source rates were daily representative rates reported to the IMF, filters the source to dates from 2012, and multiplies accounting/fee/forecast fields by names ending in _USD_Convert. The official IMF archive describes representative rates as currency units per U.S. dollar. The exact author CSV quote convention, inverse conversion, six-currency coverage, required event dates within the 30-day merge limit, and treatment of any pre-2012 Compustat rows used in the four-year lags are unresolved; do not change conversion direction or extend coverage without supported evidence.

The two I/B/E/S division-by-100 conditions compare the expanded loop macro to bare GBP tokens. Stata 18 documents that an unquoted macro value is treated as a variable; the adjacent currency-selection conditions already quote the macro. Quote the expanded macro in both comparisons in a working copy, preserving the GBP-only scaling, source variables and subsequent currency multipliers. This is a supported same-operation preparation correction, not a result of executing Code.do.

/* Create materiality varaibles */
gen mgmt_adj_amt_s_pi = mgmt_adj_amt/abs(pi)
gen aud_adj_amt_s_pi = aud_adj_amt/abs(pi)
gen perc_calculated = materiality_amt/(abs(pi))
gen mgmt_adj_pi = pi + mgmt_adj_amt
gen aud_adj_pi = pi + aud_adj_amt
gen disagreement = mgmt_adj_amt_s_pi - aud_adj_amt_s_pi
gen revt_mat_perc = materiality_amt/revt
gen revt_mat_perc_no_adj = (abs(pi)*perc)/revt

/* Create volatility measures */
egen earnings_vol = rowsd(pi pi_lag1 pi_lag2 pi_lag3)
replace earnings_vol = ln(earnings_vol)

egen cash_vol = rowsd(oancf oancf_lag1 oancf_lag2 oancf_lag3)
replace cash_vol = ln(cash_vol)

/* Create contextual factor score variable */
gen large_earnings_decrease = (pi < .25 * ((pi_lag1 + pi_lag2 + pi_lag3)/3) & pi != . & pi_lag1 != . & pi_lag2 != . & pi_lag3 != .) 
gen near_change_eps = (abs(epsincon-epsincon_lag1) <= .02 & epsincon != . & epsincon_lag1 != .)
gen small_profit = (roa > 0 & roa < .01 & roa != .)
gen small_loss = (roa < 0 & roa > -.01 & roa != .)
gen small_pos_streak = (  (pi - pi_lag1)/pi_lag1 > 0 & (pi - pi_lag1)/pi_lag1 < .03     &    (pi_lag1 - pi_lag2)/pi_lag2 > 0 & (pi_lag1 - pi_lag2)/pi_lag2 < .03     &    (pi_lag2 - pi_lag3)/pi_lag3 > 0 & (pi_lag2 - pi_lag3)/pi_lag3 < .03 ) 
gen capital_raising = (sstk > (.2*at_lag1) & sstk != . & at_lag1 != . )
gen contextual_factor_score = large_earnings_decrease + near_change_eps + small_profit + small_loss + small_pos_streak + capital_raising
	
/* Create analyst variables */
replace numest = 0 if numest == . 
replace stdev = 0 if numest == 1 
gen forecast_error = (value - meanest)
gen meet_or_beat_1cent = (forecast_error <= .01 & forecast_error >= 0)

gen analyst_adj_amt = ((value * cshpria) - nicon) - (pi - nicon)
gen analyst_adj_amt_s_pi = analyst_adj_amt/abs(pi)

gen aud_excess_adj = aud_adj_amt - analyst_adj_amt 
gen aud_excess_adj_s_pi = aud_excess_adj/abs(pi)

gen mgmt_excess_adj = mgmt_adj_amt - analyst_adj_amt
gen mgmt_excess_adj_s_pi = mgmt_excess_adj/abs(pi)

/* Create asset-scaled variables for persistence tests */
gen mgmt_exclude_s_at = mgmt_adj_amt/at_lag1
gen aud_exclude_s_at = aud_adj_amt/at_lag1
gen pi_lead1_s_at = pi_lead1/at
gen mgmt_adj_pi_s_at = mgmt_adj_pi/at_lag1
gen aud_adj_pi_s_at = aud_adj_pi/at_lag1

/* Create benchmark category variable for mlogit test */
gen benchmark_cat = 1 if pbt_benchmark == 1 & aud_adj_dummy == 0
replace benchmark_cat = 2 if pbt_benchmark == 1 & aud_adj_dummy == 1
replace benchmark_cat = 3 if pbt_benchmark == 0

/* Create variables for market return test */
gen aud_adj_pi_ps = aud_adj_pi/cshpria
gen mgmt_adj_pi_ps = mgmt_adj_pi/cshpria
gen aud_excess_adj_dummy = (aud_excess_adj > 0)

evidence.quote:
Audit Implications of Non-GAAP Reporting

                           Nicholas Hallman, Jaime Schmidt, Anne Thompson
evidence.description: The datasheet identifies the paper title and authors.

evidence.quote:
The raw data were collected from annual reports downloaded directly from Companies House and from
companies’ corporate investor relations websites. Originally, we downloaded the first year of data from
Companies House (the U.K. equivalent of the SEC’s EDGAR) between July 2014 and April 2015. Because
companies in Jersey, Guernsey, Ireland, and the Isle of Man are not required to file with Companies
House, we obtained annual reports from these companies’ investor relations websites. Between August
2016 and July 2017, we downloaded text-searchable pdfs for the first year of data from companies’
investor relations websites to facilitate data collection. We downloaded the second year of data from
companies’ investor relations websites and Companies House between June 2017 and February 2018.
We do not expect that the exact date of download impacts the reliability of the data because the source
of the data is the annual report and restatements in the U.K. are very rare. The authors and 18 research
assistants at the University of Illinois and University of Texas at Austin collected the data necessary for
this study. Other data was downloaded from Compustat Global on 6/7/2021, from I/B/E/S on
9/30/2017, from FAME in August of 2016, and from Audit Analytics on 10/30/2019. Daily stock market
data was downloaded by RAs from Yahoo Finance and Investing.com. At the Editor’s request, we hand
collected data that was missing from the archival databases to increase the sample size to the extent
possible.
evidence.description: The datasheet describes annual-report hand collection and names Compustat Global, I/B/E/S, FAME, Audit Analytics and daily market data origins.

actions.description: Follow the supplied Code.do order and named producer-consumer chain through FINAL.dta after the raw-input, software and working-root preparation is complete.
steps: Use a dedicated writable working root containing Code.do and DATA/RAW DATA plus DATA/PROC DATA; create those directories during setup because the supplied script does not create them. Set home_directory to '.' in the working copy and start batch Stata from that root.
Import HAND_COLLECTED_DATA.xlsx and create DATA/PROC DATA/FIRM_ID.dta; import the currency CSV and create 1.2.K.dta. The currency panel feeds the subsequent Compustat, FAME and I/B/E/S stages.

Run the supplied Compustat Global stage with FIRM_ID.dta and 1.2.K.dta to produce 1.2.A.dta; then the FAME stage with FIRM_ID.dta and 1.2.K.dta to produce 1.2.F.dta; the I/B/E/S stage with FIRM_ID.dta and 1.2.K.dta to produce 1.2.J.dta; and the Audit Analytics stage with FIRM_ID.dta to produce 1.2.T.dta.

Import the hand-collected workbook as the 2.1 base. Merge 1.2.A.dta by gvkey/fyear, 1.2.T.dta by isin/fyear/audit_firm_hand, 1.2.F.dta by regno/fyear with update, then 1.2.J.dta by sedol2/fyear; save 2.1.dta.

Consume 2.1.dta in the variable-construction stage, including its gvkey/fyear panel, and save 2.2.a.dta. Consume 2.2.a.dta in the final stage, apply the supplied winsor2 and dropmiss calls, and save FINAL.dta.

Keep all named inputs and branches in this order. The trace records these intermediate files as generated dependencies, not as separate external-data requirements; their schemas and upstream compatibility are still subject to the unresolved input checks.
